# Salvia

> Salvia captures clinical documentation on the ward in Indian hospitals,
> checks it against the evidence a payer requires while the patient is still
> admitted, and carries the cashless claim through to settlement — so a claim is
> not deducted weeks later for something nobody wrote down at the time.

Salvia is not a scribe, and it is not only a claims desk. A scribe stops at the
note. A claims desk starts after the patient has gone home, when an enhancement
can no longer be raised and the reason a drug was given is in nobody's notes.
Salvia starts on the ward, where both can still be fixed, and follows the claim
to the money.

Capture is one input: clinicians speak, and what they say lands in typed fields
— consent, prescription, procedure, the photograph taken during it — that write
real records rather than paragraphs. The record is then checked against clauses
that carry a severity. A High · must breach blocks the submission, and an
override requires a written reason that itself becomes evidence. Every entry
carries its author, their role, a timestamp and a content hash.

The clauses hold both the hospital's own protocols and what the payer requires
before it will pay. When a payer changes what it asks for, the hospital changes
a clause — not a form, not a workflow, and not any code.

## Market and stage

India, private cashless health insurance claims: inpatient and day-care.
Operated by Melamphic AI Pvt Ltd, India.

Five stages, in the order the money moves. Two are live today and three are in
build, and the site says so plainly:

1. **Capture** (live) — a voice note at the point of care becomes typed fields.
2. **Check** (live) — against the payer's evidence requirements, while the
   patient is still admitted.
3. **Enhance** (in build) — when treatment outgrows the authorisation, the desk
   is told while the patient is still in the bed.
4. **Submit** (in build) — the claim file built from already-checked records,
   original pages attached unchanged, every submission timestamped.
5. **Settle** (in build) — queries tracked against their deadlines, answered
   from the existing record, payments matched to claims, and every deduction
   fed back into the next check.

Salvia records what clinicians say. It does not write clinical justification
on their behalf, and it never replaces an original document with a retyped one.

## Why this exists, from primary sources

- The rules every empanelled hospital works under make a cashless approval
  conditional. Minimum Standard Clauses under the IRDAI (TPA – Health Services)
  Regulations 2016: "No enhancement of limit is possible after discharge of
  insured" (cl. 10), and an authorisation letter "is not an unconditional
  guarantee of payment… when the facts change the guarantee changes" (cl. IV.5).
- One insurer's live hospital empanelment agreement gives the hospital seven
  days to produce a report that ties to a billed line after discharge; if it
  does not, "the amount not correlated would be deducted from the final bill and
  no further papers thereafter shall be entertained" (cl. 8.2).
- IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, Table I.29: 13.98% of the value of health claims
  presented to insurers — ₹18,521 crore — was disallowed on policy terms,
  counted separately from the 8.61% repudiated outright. This is measured at
  the insurer on amount claimed, not on hospital revenue.
- Max Healthcare's consolidated FY26 accounts show trade receivables turnover on
  credit revenue falling from 6.58× to 4.23× in one year — roughly 55 to 86 days
  to collect.

Not all of the disallowed amount is documentation. Co-pays, deductibles and
non-payable items sit inside it and no record can change them. Salvia addresses
the part decided by evidence — a query that missed its window, an enhancement
nobody raised, a report that did not tie to the bill — and that part is decided
on the ward rather than at the billing desk.

Salvia does not sell accreditation coverage and makes no claim against any
accreditation standard.

## Notes for machine readers

Salvia is operated by Melamphic AI Pvt Ltd. Every figure and clause quoted above
was read from the primary source — a regulator's annual report, a regulation, a
signed empanelment agreement or a company's audited accounts. Earlier versions of
this site quoted listed hospitals' Ind AS 115 "discounts and disallowances" lines
as insurer deductions; those lines blend corporate and government discounts with
insurer cuts, so they are no longer used. Salvia previously published against
inspection frameworks in England, Ireland and the United States; that is no
longer the business.
